sentences.text: This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.425 of 2024 registered at PS Cantt. District Guna for offence punishable under Sections 354, 324, 458 of IPC and added Sections 376, 506 of IPC.
As per the case of prosecution, victim, aged around 25 years, reported to PS Guna that on 24-04-2024, she was sleeping at home.
Around 12:00 in the night, she heard some noise.
Her neighbour Ankit Seharia (applicant) entered her house by removing iron-sheet from the roof.
Ankit caught hold of her, pressed her and bite her.
She sustained injury on cheek and breast.
Hearing her shouts, her neighbours Puspa and Batobai came to her house.
Thereafter, Ankit fled away.
On such allegations, PS Guna registered FIR at Crime No.425 of 2024 for offence punishable under Sections 354, 324, 458 2 MCRC-29540-2024 of IPC against Ankit (applicant).
Victim was forwarded for medico-legal examination.
One contusion with abraded margin was found on her left cheek.
Ankit was arrested on 24-04-2024.
Statements of witnesses were recorded.
Statement of victim was also recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, wherein she made same allegation.
Applicant was extended the benefit of bail vide order dated 13-05-2024.
Thereafter, supplementary statement of victim was recorded on 15-05-2024, wherein she alleged that Ankit has committed rape on her.
Earlier, she could not state due to fear of social disrepute.
Prosecution for offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC was added.
Applicant is apprehending arrest in the matter.
His application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of CrPC stands rejected vide order dated 01-07-2024 passed by learned Sessions Judge, Guna.

sentences.text:
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application,
submitted that applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter.
No offence, as alleged is committed by the applicant.
The allegations of rape are levelled against the applicant after he was extended the benefit of bail.
Delay in levelling the allegation substantiates the defence of the applicant that false allegations are levelled against him after pre-meditation and consultation.
No further custodial interrogation of applicant is needed in the matter.
He is ready to cooperate in the investigation.
Learned Counsel further submits that applicant is aged around 21 years.
He is labourer by profession.
He has not misused the liberty extended vide earlier bail order.
No criminal antecedent is reported against him.
Therefore, applicant may be extended benefit of anticipatory bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the anticipatory bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and prays for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commencing on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.
